claim: NCEI lists seven significant volcanic events for calendar 2021: Sangay (Ecuador, 5 Mar), Pacaya (Guatemala, Mar), Soufriere St Vincent (9 Apr), Nyiragongo (DR Congo, 22 May), Stromboli (Italy, 19 May), La Palma (Spain, 19 Sep) and Semeru (Indonesia, 4 Dec)
value: 7 significant events; Americas 3, Europe 2, Africa 1, Asia 1
source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database (hazel API, JSON)
note: 'Significant' is NCEI's own filter, so this is not a count of all 2021 eruptions. The Smithsonian GVP count of 2021 eruptions could not be read (bot check blocks volcano.si.edu), so do not say '2021 had N eruptions'.

claim: NCEI records Soufriere St Vincent on 9 April 2021 at VEI 4, damage about US$325 million; Semeru on 4 December 2021 at VEI 4; La Palma on 19 September 2021 at VEI 3; Nyiragongo 22 May 2021 at VEI 2
source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database (hazel API, JSON)
note: VEI = Volcanic Explosivity Index. None of 2021's significant eruptions reached VEI 5 or above (NCEI list).

claim: Nyiragongo (DR Congo), 22 May 2021: NCEI records 32 deaths and about 5,000 houses destroyed; UN News quotes OCHA that the first eruption of lava, ash and gas destroyed houses, schools and health structures and affected water and electricity supply, and quotes an IOM spokesperson that the first eruption killed over 30 people
source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database (hazel API, JSON)
second_source: UN News, Goma evacuation (May 2021, OCHA briefing)
note: Audit fix: the 'over 30 killed' line is the IOM spokesperson quoted in the UN News piece, not OCHA; house/school/health/water line is the UN News text of the OCHA briefing. 'Houses destroyed' count per NCEI; no house count in the piece.

claim: Goma evacuation after Nyiragongo: OCHA's spokesperson said about 400,000 people were potentially affected by the evacuation order and thousands were on the move
source: UN News, Goma evacuation (May 2021, OCHA briefing)
note: IOM/other counts of displaced (higher or lower) were seen only in news summaries, so not used. Say 'potentially affected', not 'displaced'.

claim: Soufriere St Vincent: erupted 9 April 2021 after being dormant since 1979; ash blanketed the island and about 16,000 residents were evacuated; the entire population of the main island lacked clean water and electricity (UN spokesperson citing OCHA)
value: ~16,000 evacuated; island-wide water and power loss
source: UN News, 'Volcanic eruption leaves entire population of Saint Vincent without clean water' (12 Apr 2021, citing OCHA)
note: Same UN piece says about 20,000 evacuees needed shelter: the two figures differ in the same article (16,000 residents evacuated vs 20,000 evacuees in need). Name the source for whichever is used.

claim: Soufriere St Vincent: ash and lava flows hampered movement of people and goods and hit livelihoods in the north of the island, including banana farming
source: UN News, 'Volcanic eruption leaves entire population of Saint Vincent without clean water' (12 Apr 2021, citing OCHA)
note: Environmental impact on agriculture and water. Quote kept under 15 words by paraphrase.

claim: La Palma (Cumbre Vieja, Tajogaite), Canary Islands: eruption began 19 September 2021 and lasted 85 days; lava flow field about 1.8 x 10^8 m3 over about 12 km2; tephra blanket about 2.3 x 10^7 m3; about 3,000 buildings destroyed and several thousand people evacuated
source: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 25, 14591 (2025), Volatile emissions during the 2021 Cumbre Vieja (La Palma) eruption
second_source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database (hazel API, JSON)
note: NCEI gives 1,345 houses destroyed and US$924 million damage, 1 death: a different count from the ACP paper's ~3,000 buildings (buildings vs houses; ACP cites Copernicus EMSR546). Name the source.

claim: La Palma 2021 gases: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI satellite data give total emissions of 1.8 +/- 0.2 Mt SO2, 19.4 +/- 1.8 Mt CO2, 0.05 Mt HCl and 0.013 Mt HF over the eruption
source: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 25, 14591 (2025), Volatile emissions during the 2021 Cumbre Vieja (La Palma) eruption
note: The paper says these emissions are non-negligible against Spain's and Europe's annual inventories. An earlier estimate cited in the same paper (Milford 2023) is about 1.84 Mt SO2.

claim: La Palma plume: volcanic gases were injected between 1,000 and 6,000 m above sea level and carried over North Africa, Europe and, on several occasions, across the Atlantic to the Caribbean
source: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 25, 14591 (2025), Volatile emissions during the 2021 Cumbre Vieja (La Palma) eruption
note: Regional-to-transcontinental air-quality reach; plume height is the main uncertainty in satellite SO2 totals.

claim: Scale check (our arithmetic): La Palma's 1.8 Mt SO2 is about one tenth of Pinatubo 1991's nearly 20 Mt SO2 (USGS), and Pinatubo cooled the globe about 0.5 C for 1991-93; no source read gives a global cooling for 2021
source: Our calculation: ACP 2025 (1.8 Mt) / USGS FS 113-97 (about 20 Mt, ledger GEO-04 V060)
note: Do NOT claim 2021 eruptions changed global climate. Impact was regional (air quality, ash, land). 'Corrected' = common assumption that big eruptions cool the globe does not follow here. Our own ratio, labelled as such.

claim: Fagradalsfjall (Reykjanes, Iceland): the eruption began 19 March 2021, the first on the Reykjanes Peninsula in about 800 years, in Geldingadalir valley from a 180 m fissure, and ended 18 September 2021
source: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences 23, 3147 (2023), Lava flow hazard modeling during the 2021 Fagradalsfjall eruption
note: Not in NCEI's significant list for 2021. Iceland's own Met Office bulletins were not opened.

claim: Fagradalsfjall final lava field: bulk volume 150.8 x 10^6 m3 over 4.85 km2, maximum thickness 124 m; the site is near Reykjavik and the international airport (the paper: 'backyard of the capital')
source: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences 23, 3147 (2023), Lava flow hazard modeling during the 2021 Fagradalsfjall eruption
note: Audit fix: 'within sight of' replaced; the paper only says backyard of the capital and the airport. Gas pollution at Fagradalsfjall (SO2 tonnes per day) could not be read at the Smithsonian GVP (blocked), so no gas figure is claimed.

claim: Fukutoku-Oka-no-Ba (Ogasawara/Izu-Bonin, Japan) submarine eruption 13-15 August 2021 sent floating pumice about 1,300 km west; it reached Okinawa about two months later
source: Scientific Reports 12 (2022), Coastal ecological impacts from pumice rafts
second_source: Scientific Reports 13, 3945 (2023), Projection of August 2021 pumice dispersion
note: Second paper (model of the dispersal) page was read for title and date only; its figures were not extracted.

claim: Pumice impact on Okinawa's coast: northern Okinawa has coral reefs, mangroves and a World Natural Heritage Site (2021); the paper reports early ecosystem changes from pumice stranding on beaches, in estuaries and mangroves and across fringing reefs, and says pumice drifts obstruct fishing and ship traffic
source: Scientific Reports 12 (2022), Coastal ecological impacts from pumice rafts
note: Pumice rafts also carry marine organisms (barnacle Lepas, bryozoans were found on stranded pumice) so they spread species: a regional ecological effect both ways.

claim: Semeru (Java, Indonesia), 4 December 2021: NCEI records VEI 4 with 45 deaths in one field and 51 in another, 9 missing, about 2,970 houses destroyed and about US$20 million damage
source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database (hazel API, JSON)
note: Audit fix: removed 'the agent is pyroclastic flows': the NCEI record only carries agent code 'T' and the file holds no legend, so the agent is unsupported. Inside the NCEI record 'deathsTotal' is 45 and 'deaths' is 51, so the database disagrees with itself. Use 'about 50' or avoid. No second official source (BNPB, OCHA) was opened.

claim: The 15 January 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption (VEI 6) is NOT a 2021 event; do not put it in this answer
source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database (ledger GEO-04 V064)
note: A common trap: candidates add Tonga to 2021 answers.
